note: 50 cuts, 11 transcript lines. Every cut is one shot with its own number and times. Two speakers, each under one name all reel long: the flashback and the echo are still 'bride', and the ex at the party is still 'bride'. Shot 44 morphs into real footage and 45–50 are phone video, so all seven are live action. Captions are described, never copied.

output.logline: A groom is dumped at the altar for a richer man, turns his heartbreak into a two-year hustle, and when his ex finds him again surrounded by admirers in a penthouse he tells her he's 'fully booked'.
output.style: 3D animated CG: rounded big-eyed characters, warm cinematic light

hook.mechanic: Cold open mid-climax: 'I do' answered by a screamed 'HELL NO!' in extreme close-up, 6 shots in the first 2.3 s, ring thrown and bouncing on the floor, public betrayal ('I'm marrying him!') - instant conflict, no setup.

beats.summary: HOOK: altar humiliation. 'I do' -> bride screams 'HELL NO!', throws the ring, announces 'I'm marrying him!' -> groom 'What?!'
Abandonment: bride leaves with the rival in a luxury car; groom left alone at the altar, picks up the ring.
Wound: puts on the ring, flashback 'I can't wait to spend forever with you', echoing 'forever with you' over his blank face.
MONTAGE: wordless grind - laptop, camera, typing, packing orders across ever-bigger rooms/warehouses, walking warehouse aisles, then black suit, penthouse, skyline.
Reversal: ex and rival at a penthouse party spot him - 'Nate? Nate? Huh?!' - snap zoom on her shocked face.
Payoff: Nate by the glass, women gather around him, push-in to his smug smile: 'Sorry, I'm fully booked.'
Real-life tag: CG Nate morphs into the real creator; rapid handheld lifestyle flexes (car, balcony, apartment, supercars) under a caption.

montage.description: Wordless, music-driven rise montage (11.7 s, 24 shots, median 0.3 s): hand on laptop, typing, camera to lens, POV typing, online store page, rapid match-cut taping/packing of parcels as the background swaps from bedroom to stockroom to big warehouse (one bg shows a rising bar chart), walking toward camera down warehouse aisles with match-cut background swaps, then a tracking shot of him in a black suit walking through a penthouse onto a night-skyline balcony.

why_it_works: Hook starts at the peak: the betrayal happens in the first second, with a screamed line and a jarring ECU - no context needed to feel it.
Universal revenge/glow-up arc (humiliation -> grind -> success -> ex regrets) in under 45 s; the viewer stays to see the payback promised by the setup.
Ultra-fast opening cuts (6 shots in 2.3 s) then slower emotional shots - pace mirrors shock then grief.
Repeated echo 'forever with you' turns the wound into motivation and bridges into the montage.
Montage is wordless, match-cut and musical: the same pose in ever-bigger settings shows scale of success with zero exposition.
'2 YEARS LATER' card + mirrored party scene sets up the reversal; the payoff line is short, quotable and smug.
